title: Prompting the Benefit of the Doubt: The Joint Effect of Auditor-Client Social Bonds and Measurement Uncertainty on Audit Adjustments

scopes.description: Reproduce the reported experimental analyses using the authors’ observed participant data, required data preparation, embedded SPSS analyses and the documented manual experimental instruments.

requirements.description: Observed participant-level data required by the reported experimental analyses, including the z-Tree task outputs and coded questionnaire/trivia measures or a compatible author-prepared analysis dataset. The code names SocialBond, Uncertainty, ManipulationCheck1–3, QuestionsCorrect, and a dependent-variable placeholder, but the assigned package contains no observations or verified compatible data route.

routes.location: Authors’ retained experimental data (specific repository/access route not identified)
routes.description: The datasheet states that both authors have full access to the data and will retain it for six years. It gives no delivery route, file format, field inventory, sample/eligibility details, or coverage evidence. Request an author-prepared analysis dataset or the underlying data with its conversion procedure.

software.name: SPSS Statistics
software.description: The datasheet says SPSS was used for the listed t-tests, factorial ANOVA and correlations. No version is specified. A bounded PATH lookup found none of the checked SPSS launcher names; this does not establish that no licensed or GUI installation exists.

issues.description: The datasheet says complete collection/processing details are in the article and that the raw-to-analysis program or step-by-step replacement is at the end of the document. The supplied ending contains statistical-test syntax and contrast weights, but no supported conversion/coding procedure for producing the analysis dataset from z-Tree output and paper responses. The cited article is not part of this assigned package.

The SPSS syntax includes a generic DependentVariable placeholder and refers readers to the manuscript and Appendix B for variable choices and definitions. The manuscript and a table/footnote-to-procedure mapping are not in this package, so the supplied syntax cannot yet be mapped to every reported analysis.

evidence.description: The datasheet identifies the experiment data as z-Tree output plus paper post-experimental questionnaires and gives the historical session dates.
evidence.quote: Data were downloaded from z-tree immediately after each session.

evidence.description: The authors state that they have full access to the collected data.
evidence.quote: Both authors have full access to the data.

evidence.description: The datasheet places sample/data-processing details in the article and says the raw-to-analysis program or detailed steps are provided at the end of this document.
evidence.quote: This information is provided at the end of this document.

evidence.description: The datasheet contains actual SPSS syntax for independent-sample t-tests, factorial ANOVA, correlations and an ANOVA control analysis.
evidence.quote: We relied on SPSS to estimate the 2 × 2 analysis of variance (ANOVA), including simple effects, underlying many of our results.

evidence.quote: Participants worked through the instructions at their own speed and were required to answer each comprehension check question correctly before continuing.

actions.description: Request the authors’ observed experimental dataset and the information needed to establish a compatible analysis input.
steps: Ask whether the authors can supply the analysis-ready participant-level dataset used for the paper or, if they expect raw-data preparation, the underlying z-Tree outputs and entered/coded questionnaire and trivia records.

Request a data dictionary, field coding, participant/session identifiers, inclusion/exclusion rules, the relevant sample history and exact file format. The historical session dates are documented, but do not establish file coverage or sample eligibility.
Do not recruit new subjects or fabricate outcomes to replace the missing historical data.
validation: After receipt, inspect the data using a bounded format-aware metadata/readability check and compare actual columns to the SPSS variables and author-supplied data dictionary.
Confirm the dataset contains the documented historical sample and all cases used by the reported analyses; a one-row metadata probe will not establish population coverage.

actions.description: Obtain the missing raw-to-analysis instructions, exact analysis mapping and SPSS details before attempting the supplied procedures.
steps: Request the manuscript sections cited for subject eligibility/selection, exclusions, variable construction and analysis definitions, including the Appendix B/footnote 17 mapping for the generic dependent-variable syntax.

Request the actual raw-to-analysis program or a complete step-by-step conversion/coding recipe for z-Tree data and paper responses, including merge keys, recodes, exclusions and the construction of QuestionsCorrect and all model variables.

Request the SPSS version, import instructions, expected analysis-file path/format and a table/footnote-to-procedure map covering all reported analyses. Confirm whether the supplied syntax covers each reported test.
validation: Check that the received preparation code or recipe produces every input field used by the SPSS syntax without changing the original experimental observations or selection rules.
Check SPSS version and import behavior, resolve every DependentVariable use, and map each paper result to its supplied procedure.

actions.description: Once the data, conversion instructions and variable mapping are available, run the embedded statistical procedures in their documented order and compare outputs with the article.
steps: Prepare or import the author-provided analysis dataset using the received conversion recipe; skip raw preparation only if the authors confirm the supplied file is the analysis-ready dataset for these results.
Resolve each DependentVariable placeholder from the author’s table mapping before copying the syntax blocks unchanged into a working SPSS syntax file.
Run the T-TEST, UNIANOVA, CORRELATIONS and trivia-control UNIANOVA procedures for their specified outcomes, and apply the stated contrast weights to the analyses for Tables 3 and 4.
Use the author-specified SPSS version and compare resulting sample counts, test statistics and outputs with the corresponding tables and footnotes.
validation: Verify syntax/import completion, sample counts and result-to-table mapping against author documentation; record execution evidence only after a separately authorized run.

review_notes: The data sheet contains substantive SPSS syntax embedded in a PDF, so has_code is true even though no standalone .sps file is supplied. The static code scan did not recognize this document-embedded syntax; content inspection controls the assessment.

The experimental-materials PDF supplies participant instructions, Z-Tree interface screenshots and paper questionnaires. These manual materials are credited. The data sheet’s z-Tree reference documents historical data capture; it does not create a current requirement to run a new experiment when the target is the authors’ historical observations.
No analysis_only scope is supported because the release includes no compatible analysis dataset. The empirical target requires historical participant data, so data_required remains true.
No explicit author data/code URL is present in the assigned documents. The author-held data route is therefore retained as unverified; no data download or contact was made.
